title: Improving Adversarial Robustness of Attribution via Implicit Regularization
claim: A training-induced regularizer flattens parameter curvature, which via curvature bounds transfers to input space and reduces sensitivity of explanations to attack.
layout: 3 zones, left-to-right, red parameter and blue input space split by dashed line
description: A wide figure split into a pink left region for parameter space and a light-blue right region for input space, divided by a vertical dashed line. On the left, a red box labeled Implicit Curvature Regularization (Section C.1) connects by curved arrows to two small loss-landscape sketches. The top sketch shows a large learning rate on a wide, shallow parabola, which gives low parameter curvature. The bottom sketch shows a small learning rate on a narrow, steep parabola, which gives high parameter curvature. Both feed arrows into a central red-to-blue gradient box, Input-Parameter Curvature Bounds (Proposition 1). From there, two arrows lead to rows of attribution heatmaps. In the top row, the attribution map changes little under attack, which is labeled Low Attribution Sensitivity. In the bottom row, the map collapses into a single yellow blob, which is labeled High Attribution Sensitivity. A fish photo, labeled Input Sample, sits at the far right. Red and blue text marks the parameter and input spaces, and green and magenta mark curvature and learning rate.
caption: Implicit Regularization; An Efficient Alternative to Attribution Robustness. This figure summarizes the key mechanisms underlying attribution robustness. In CNNs and MLPs, training near the edge of stability biases SGD toward flatter regions of the parameter landscape, while smaller learning rates favor sharper minima. By linking established results on SGD implicit regularization with parameter–input curvature transfer ([ref]), we show that flatter parameter regions yield more robust gradient-based attributions. For ViTs with softmax attention, robustness is instead governed by attention entropy ([ref]). Finally, we demonstrate that implicit regularization can also improve attention-based attribution robustness when softmax is replaced by \kernelized attention in ViT-B/16.
abstract: The adversarial robustness of attributions is a fundamental requirement for reliable explainability in deep learning, yet existing approaches typically rely on computationally expensive explicit regularization. In this work, we show that attribution robustness can arise implicitly from the learning dynamics of standard stochastic gradient descent. We theoretically motivate this effect through connections between parameter-space and input-space curvature, and validate it across architectures, datasets, and attribution methods, with negligible computational overhead. In contrast, we prove that such robustness gains often does not transfer to attention-based attribution under softmax normalization, due to inherent entropy constraints, and we validate this limitation experimentally. Finally, we show that replacing softmax attention with kernel-based attention restores the robustness gains in transformer models. Our results highlight learning dynamics as a principled and practical mechanism for robust explainability, and reveal fundamental limitations of attention-based attribution under normalization.
